source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check security mode could be change
1. Asserted TPM physical presence by on-board jumper or switch
2. Power on SUT and enter into F1 setup.
3. Navigate to Security page to enable secure boot and TPM function.
4. Change Security Boot mode to another mode .
5. Save and reboot system.
6. Check Security mode has been changed.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. Security mode can be changed successfully.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Security mode: change the ROT security mode. Agent can only read current state from OS sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "mokutil --sb-state 2>&1; dmesg 2>&1 | grep -iE 'rot|pfr|secure' | tail -n 20 2>&1"; the security-mode change requires the TPM physical-presence jumper/switch and BIOS F1 setup navigation by an operator.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the current secure-boot/ROT-related dmesg lines so the user confirms the state before an operator changes the ROT security mode in BIOS.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: ROT security-mode change needs physical TPM-presence assertion + BIOS setup - operator required; do not auto-run.

original_test_intent: Use the platform physical-presence control and BIOS Security page to change an approved ROT/secure-boot/TPM security mode, reboot, and verify that the intended final mode is active without an unintended boot or key-state regression.
original_method: An engineer asserts the documented on-board physical-presence jumper or switch, enters F1 BIOS setup, enables the specified security prerequisites, selects the approved destination mode, saves and reboots, then visually confirms BIOS state while OS and management evidence are collected.
manual_activity: The source makes physical jumper/switch assertion, F1 BIOS navigation, security-setting changes and final BIOS observation part of the core acceptance path. These are engineer operations; OS evidence collection does not replace them.
required_inputs: Exact platform, BIOS, TPM and ROT/PFR identities
Named source and destination security modes and required secure-boot/TPM state
Physical-presence jumper/switch location, asserted/restored positions and ESD/power procedure
Key, measured-boot, disk-unlock and attestation impact
OOB/KVM access, recovery/rollback and one-user approval
safety_requirements: Do not guess 'another mode' or alter physical-presence/security state without the approved transition.
Preserve TPM ownership, secure-boot keys and recovery material; never clear or re-own TPM as a workaround.
Verify maintenance isolation and KVM/OOB recovery before save/reboot.
Stop on unexpected key, boot, attestation or management-state change; do not automatically retry.
agent_execution_scope: Capture immutable pre/post platform, BIOS/ROT/TPM, secure-boot, OS, BMC and SEL evidence around the engineer's actions.
Run only approved read-only OS queries and compare the observed final state with the named destination.
Report evidence and tool results without claiming the physical or BIOS actions or setting the formal verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve the exact transition and recovery plan.
Perform and document the physical-presence and BIOS operations, including restoration of the jumper/switch.
Confirm the authoritative BIOS/security state and issue PASS or FAIL.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: mokutil may report OS-visible Secure Boot state and selected dmesg lines may provide supporting context, but neither proves the ROT mode, TPM enablement or physical-presence transition; applicability must be confirmed for the selected OS.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain the read-only mokutil check where supported and add only vendor-documented, platform-specific readback. Do not invent a command that substitutes for the physical and BIOS sequence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The physical-presence, F1 setup, save/reboot and 5/5-minute source fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.status: RETAIN ORIGINAL PHYSICAL/BIOS METHOD; ADD TRACEABLE READBACK
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use an approved change manifest naming the before/after modes, record jumper/switch and BIOS screens, and correlate them with supported Secure Boot, TPM and ROT/PFR readback after reboot.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the exact board, BIOS, TPM and ROT/PFR implementation.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record board, BIOS, BMC, ROT/PFR, TPM, OS and mokutil versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Owner/vendor board service manual, BIOS security guide and ROT/PFR/TPM recovery procedure.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds explicit transition identity, recovery gates and correlated evidence without replacing manual physical presence or BIOS observation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; the physical and BIOS acceptance remains mandatory.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Platform-specific modes, control map, policy and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: OS-visible Secure Boot state alone cannot establish the complete security-mode transition.

project_override_considerations: The project may choose the authorized from/to mode and evidence tools. Missing selections make execution not ready, not permanently BLOCKED; an automated BMC setting is not an equivalent substitute unless the project explicitly changes the method and coverage.
expected_evidence: Approved transition, platform/firmware identity, key impact, recovery and authorization
Before/after physical-presence position and BIOS Security-page images with timestamps
Save/reboot/POST/boot evidence and supported TPM/Secure Boot/ROT readback
BMC/SEL/host health, restored control state and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently asks for a mode change; 'another mode' is underspecified but not internally contradictory. It is an execution-readiness input.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The required operation is understandable. V3.1 treats the unnamed project transition and recovery data as prerequisites rather than permanent blockage.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retain its manual-operation warning but reject read-only OS output as proof of the full transition.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retain all security and recovery gates but change permanent BLOCKED to NOT READY under V3.1.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Classifies the case MANUAL ONLY because human physical and BIOS actions are the core test, while keeping evidence assistance separate.

review_improvement: Names the authoritative transition and distinguishes manual acceptance from agent-collected supporting evidence, avoiding both a false automation claim and a permanent block for project-specific inputs.
independent_technical_reasoning: This is not merely a manual setup followed by an automated core: the requested security-mode change itself requires physical presence, interactive BIOS modification and human visual confirmation. Therefore MANUAL ONLY is more accurate than the historical PARTIAL label; agent evidence support does not change that classification.
